newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaueble - room for EMU manoeuvre restricted.
newsitem.headline: Schaueble - room for EMU manoeuvre restricted.

text.p: Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, said that in the run-up to Europe's Economic and Monetary Union there was "less room for manoeuvre" on EMU criteria than is actually set out by the Maastricht Treaty.

Schaeuble, speaking at a jobs summit, said this was because Germany in particular in the past had always insisted on strict adherence to the criteria, and that it would be dangerous for it to change its tone now.
"All efforts must be made to fulfil the criteria so that EMU can start on time," said Schaeuble.

In order to join currency union, countries face strict entry criteria, including low budget deficits, government debt and stable exchange rates. Currency union is scheduled to begin on January 1,1999.
German policy makers have generally favoured a strict interpretation of the entry criteria and argue this was necessary to ensure the stability of the new currency, the euro.
Schaeuble said the Treaty as it stands had been ratified in Germany and that "we should stick to those commitments already made in the Treaty."
He added that public debts across Europe would have to be reduced regardless of EMU and that he saw "no contradiction between the fulfilment of the criteria and the fight against joblessness."
